HelpPage.faqWhatIsYouduAnswer: YouDu is a platform that connects clients and specialists in the UAE. Clients post tasks, and specialists respond with offers for their services.
HelpPage.faqHowToRegisterQuestion: How do I sign up for YouDu?
HelpPage.faqHowToRegisterAnswer: Click "Log in" in the top right corner, then choose "Sign up". You can sign up with your email or with a Google or Apple account.
HelpPage.faqIsItFreeAnswer: Signing up and posting tasks is free. Specialists pay a commission only after a task has been successfully completed.
HelpPage.faqHowToCreateTaskQuestion: How do I post a task?
HelpPage.faqHowToCreateTaskAnswer: Click "Create task", describe what you need, and set your budget and deadline. Once it is published, specialists will start sending you offers.
HelpPage.faqHowToChooseSpecialistQuestio: How do I choose a specialist?
HelpPage.faqHowToChooseSpecialistAnswer: Review the profiles of the specialists who sent offers, along with their ratings, reviews, and portfolios. Pick the best fit and assign them to your task.
HelpPage.faqWorkNotDoneQuestion: What if the specialist didn't do the work?
HelpPage.faqWorkNotDoneAnswer: Contact our support team through the "Support" section. We will help resolve the dispute.
HelpPage.faqCanCancelTaskAnswer: Yes, you can cancel a task before a specialist is assigned. After that, it can only be canceled by agreement with the specialist.
HelpPage.faqHowToBecomeSpecialistQuestio: How do I become a specialist on YouDu?
HelpPage.faqHowToBecomeSpecialistAnswer: When signing up, choose "I'm a specialist", complete your profile, add a portfolio, and start sending offers on tasks.
HelpPage.faqHowToGetMoreOrdersQuestion: How can I get more jobs?
HelpPage.faqHowToGetMoreOrdersAnswer: Complete your profile in full, add photos of your work to your portfolio, get verified, and collect positive reviews.
HelpPage.faqWhatIsCommissionAnswer: The commission is 10-15% of the order amount. The exact rate depends on the service category.
HelpPage.faqHowToWithdrawQuestion: How do I withdraw my earnings?
HelpPage.faqHowToWithdrawAnswer: Go to "Payouts" in your profile settings, add a payout method, and request a payout.
HelpPage.faqIsPaymentSafeQuestion: Is it safe to pay through YouDu?
HelpPage.faqIsPaymentSafeAnswer: Yes, all payments are protected. Money is released to the specialist only after the client confirms the work is done.
HelpPage.faqPaymentMethodsAnswer: Bank cards (Visa, Mastercard), Apple Pay, and Google Pay. Cash payment is available in some categories.
HelpPage.faqAvoidScammersQuestion: How do I protect myself from scammers?
HelpPage.faqAvoidScammersAnswer: Work only through the platform, don't send money directly, and check specialists' ratings and reviews.

BaraholkaPage.safety1Text: Malls, metro station halls, tower lobbies with security. All of these places have cameras. If the seller refuses to meet at all, that tells you everything.
BaraholkaPage.safety2Text: Cash in dirhams at the handover. No prepayment for a “booking”, “reservation”, or “delivery”, no matter how convincing the reason sounds.
BaraholkaPage.safety3Text: No bank asks for a code to send you money. Codes are only needed to take money out. A request to read one out is always a scam attempt.
BaraholkaPage.safety4Text: A fake “payment successful” image takes a minute to make. Check that the money arrived in your own banking app, not on the other person’s screen.
BaraholkaPage.safety5Title: iPhones only with iCloud signed out
BaraholkaPage.safety5Text: A phone locked to someone else’s Apple ID becomes a brick. Check the settings in front of the seller and verify the IMEI with *#06#.
BaraholkaPage.faq1Question: Is there an Avito equivalent in Dubai?
BaraholkaPage.faq1Answer: There’s no direct equivalent: in the UAE, that role is split across several platforms. Feature-wise, the closest is Dubizzle, the country’s largest classifieds board with search and filters. In spirit, Telegram flea markets are closer: private sellers only, no sign-up, no fees. Russian-speaking residents usually use both.
BaraholkaPage.faq2Question: Where can I buy used furniture in Dubai?
BaraholkaPage.faq2Answer: The main sources are Telegram flea markets, Dubizzle, and Facebook Marketplace. Most offers appear at the end of the school year and before summer, when expats leave the country and sell off entire apartments. It’s also worth checking your building’s chats: furniture is often given away for free there because hauling it away costs more.
BaraholkaPage.faq3Question: What is a Telegram flea market?
BaraholkaPage.faq3Answer: It’s a group chat where members post listings for their personal belongings. The group charges no fees, doesn’t hold money, and doesn’t guarantee deals: the buyer and seller agree directly. No sign-up is needed — just a Telegram account.
BaraholkaPage.faq4Question: How can I give things away for free in Dubai?
BaraholkaPage.faq4Answer: The easiest way is to post a “free to a good home” listing in a flea market group or your building’s chat. Items get picked up within hours, especially kids’ things and furniture. If you have a lot of bulky items, it’s cheaper to hire a truck to haul them away than to deal with each person separately.
BaraholkaPage.faq5Question: Is it safe to buy second-hand in the UAE?
BaraholkaPage.faq5Answer: Yes, as long as the deal happens in person and the money changes hands together with the item. Almost every scam starts where the item and the payment are separated in time: a prepayment to a courier, a payment link, a request to read out an SMS code. If you do lose money, you can file a report online through the Dubai Police eCrime platform.
BaraholkaPage.faq6Question: Do I need to register to sell something?
BaraholkaPage.faq6Answer: Not in Telegram flea markets — you only need a Telegram account. Dubizzle and Facebook Marketplace require registration. None of these platforms charge fees on private listings.
